mainEntity.name: Does everyone need aligners before a smile makeover?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Whether aligners are appropriate before a smile makeover depends entirely on the individual's dental presentation and cosmetic goals. For some patients, existing tooth positions are well-suited to direct cosmetic treatment without prior alignment. For others, correcting alignment first may lead to a more conservative, natural-looking, and durable outcome. A clinical assessment by a qualified dentist is the only way to determine which approach is most appropriate for your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: How long does aligner treatment typically take before cosmetic work can begin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment duration varies considerably between individuals, depending on the complexity of the alignment issues being addressed. Some cases may be completed within a few months, whilst others may take considerably longer. After aligner treatment concludes, a settling period is usually observed before cosmetic work begins. Your dental team will give you a realistic indication of expected timescales based on your specific clinical needs during your consultation.

mainEntity.name: Will aligners affect the shade of my teeth before veneers or whitening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aligners themselves do not change the colour or shade of teeth. If teeth whitening is part of your smile makeover plan, your dentist will advise on the most appropriate timing — typically after orthodontic treatment is complete and before any bonding or porcelain restorations are placed, as whitening does not affect the shade of restorative materials. The sequence of whitening within a smile makeover plan should always be discussed and agreed with your dental team.

mainEntity.name: Can aligners fix bite problems as well as straighten teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pro aligners are primarily designed to address tooth position within the dental arch. Some mild bite irregularities may be improved during aligner treatment, but more complex bite problems — such as significant skeletal discrepancies — may require specialist orthodontic assessment or combined orthodontic and restorative approaches. If your dentist identifies a bite concern during your assessment, they will advise whether aligner treatment alone is likely to be sufficient or whether additional evaluation is recommended.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to have cosmetic dental work without straightening teeth first?

acceptedAnswer.text: For many patients, cosmetic dental treatments are carried out successfully without prior orthodontic work. Whether this is appropriate depends on the degree of misalignment present, the type of cosmetic treatment planned, and the clinical judgement of the treating dentist. In some cases, skipping alignment may mean that more tooth preparation is required for restorations, or that the final aesthetic result is less symmetrical than it might otherwise have been. These considerations should be discussed openly with your clinician.

mainEntity.name: What happens if teeth move after a smile makeover has been completed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Teeth can shift over time regardless of whether orthodontic treatment has been carried out previously. Wearing retainers as advised after any orthodontic treatment — including aligner therapy — is the primary way to maintain tooth positions. After cosmetic work such as veneers or bonding has been placed, it is especially important to protect that investment by following retention guidance carefully. Regular dental check-ups also allow your clinician to monitor for any changes in tooth position over time.
